newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputies adopt disputed immigration bill.
newsitem.headline: French deputies adopt disputed immigration bill.

text.p: The French National Assembly approved on Tuesday a controversial bill to clamp down on illegal immigration which had prompted widespread protests by artists, intellectuals and leftist parties.

The lower house adopted the slightly-modified bill at its second reading, and the proposal was due to go before the Senate on Wednesday for final approval. Under the modified bill, foreigners who are seriously ill cannot be expelled.
Left-wing parties have already pledged to appeal against the bill, if it becomes law, to the Constitutional Council.

"This text is a very serious attack on the rights of the individual, the right to live together as a family, and it jeopardises France's universal values as far as hospitality and integration go," Communist deputy Andre Gerin said.
Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said his bill was necessary and that it reconciled "efficiency and individual rights".

The bill introduces articles to immigration regulations that will allow police to keep passports or travel documents of illegal immigrants, who are said by authorities to often destroy their documents when caught in order to avoid being sent home.
